episodes.203139: A new multi-day plume of monsoon moisture advected northward into New Mexico between an upper level trough over the southern Baja Peninsula and an upper high over the south-central CONUS. Daily rounds of afternoon thunderstorms producing heavy rain developing over the mountains of New Mexico before moving over surrounding lower elevations through the evening resulted in several events of flash flooding and isolated reports of large hail. Rainfall rates of 4 inches per hour totaling 2 inches in 30 minutes produced flash flooding in Magdalena on July 20th. The Cochiti Golf Course experienced flash flooding July 21st. The highest coverage of thunderstorms during this period occurred July 22nd with thunderstorms moving over the Ruidoso area burn scars just after sunset. Flash flooding and debris flows on and below the South Fork and Salt burn scars resulted in brief road closures. The Albuquerque metro experienced flash flooding from heavy rainfall rates of 2 inches per hour totaling 1 to 1.50 inches in 30 minutes over the North Valley neighborhood. Finally, thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall on July 24th directly over the South Fork burn scar totaling just over 2 inches produced flash flooding and debris flows down Cedar Creek and the Rio Ruidoso to Ruidoso Downs.
episodes.203996: A weak system provided just enough energy to trigger isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms. Given limited moisture, this activity was fairly high based in nature resulting in activity which produced instances of strong to severe wind gusts.
episodes.204075: A severe thunderstorm produced winds to 60 mph in Centennial Colorado.
episodes.204093: Severe wind gusts from thunderstorms mainly affected areas around Fort Peck Lake.
episodes.204140: A cluster of strong thunderstorms developed in north central Alabama during the early to mid afternoon hours. One of the thunderstorms produced gusty winds strong enough to lean a power pole over causing a power outage in a section of Huntsville.
episodes.204141: A small cluster of strong thunderstorms dropped south-southeast through far northeast Alabama during the mid evening hours. Gusty outflow winds knocked down a tree near Henegar in Jackson County.
episodes.204339: Explosive convection developed around 4 pm near I-80 near Hays, developing into a more organized MCS that surged south between 7 pm and 10 PM.
episodes.204442: Heavy rainfall of 1-2 inches over Medano Pass, within Great Sand Dunes National Park, triggered a debris flow and excess runoff over Medano Pass Primitive Road.
episodes.204520: Very hot temperatures on the afternoon of the 21st allowed for a few isolated thunderstorms to develop across portions of the South Plains, and extreme southern Texas Panhandle. Several of these storms produced severe wind gusts as they collapsed. One storm that affected Quitaque (Briscoe County) caused a roof to be blown off of a house.
episodes.204782: Upslope flow, differential heating, and vorticity maxima in the weak flow aloft led to the development of a few thunderstorms in West Texas. These storms generally began in the higher terrain and eventually moved into the Permian Basin before dissipating. One thunderstorm managed to produce a 64 mph wind gust near Crane.
episodes.204783: Upslope flow, differential heating, and upper-level vorticity maxima in the weak flow aloft led to the development of scattered thunderstorms in West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. These storms generally began in the higher terrain and moved northeast. The low levels were fairly dry, which allowed for a couple of storms to produce severe downburst winds.
episodes.204825: A summertime pattern continued over the area with scattered thunderstorms. There were several reports of strong wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.204899: A trough extended across the local area, and an area of low pressure formed along the trough axis and retrograded into the Gulf of America during this period. Waves of heavy, slow moving storms produced localized flooding rainfall. A few stronger storms produced gusty wet downbursts.
episodes.204900: A trough extended across the local area, and an area of low pressure formed along the trough axis and retrograded into the Gulf of America during this period. Waves of heavy, slow moving storms produced localized flooding rainfall. A few stronger storms produced gusty wet downbursts.
episodes.205120: A moist and unstable summer airmass led to the development of scattered afternoon thunderstorms, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.205204: A few thunderstorms moved through the Brainerd Lakes area into Aitkin and St. Louis counties during the afternoon hours of the 22nd in association with a warm front moving through the region. A few of the storms produced wind damage to trees in the area and heavy rainfall led to ponding water on an area golf course.
episodes.205552: Two areas of storms developed during the evening hours and continued into the overnight in north central and south central Kansas. Strong and damaging winds were the main hazard with estimated wind gusts up to 75 mph. There was damage to trees and powerlines reported. A semi trailer was blown over on Interstate 70 as well. A few of the storms had hail from nickel to quarter size. These storms were efficient rainfall producers with flooding in the western portions of Saline County which closed many roadways as 7.45 inches fell in Brookville.
episodes.205610: Weak sea breeze flow over the area resulted in the interaction of multiple afternoon sea breeze and outflow-enhanced boundaries that favored the brief spin-up of landspout near Nocatee in DeSoto County.
episodes.205887: Strong thunderstorms produced a severe wind gust in Dewey County during the evening.
episodes.205889: Isolated strong storms moving across the area generated nickel sized hail in Murdo and an estimated 60 mph wind gust near the town of Frederick.
episodes.205934: Thunderstorms developed over northern South Dakota and southern North Dakota as a surface low and inverted trough moved through the area. The majority of the severe weather remained over South Dakota, while only one storm became severe over North Dakota. This storm produced one inch diameter hail south of Bismarck in Burleigh County, and 71 mph wind gusts at the Mandan Airport in Morton County.
episodes.205989: A few thunderstorms developed and became severe and produced some tree damage and small hail.
episodes.205997: A strong upper high over the southeast US and a trough approaching the west coast streamed deep moisture into the Borderland with a low level surface trough located through far west Texas into eastern New Mexico. Slow moving storms brought heavy rainfall and flash flooding to the Anthony and Socorro areas.
episodes.206226: Isolated thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours across southeast Georgia near a stationary front and a weak area of low pressure. One storm in Bulloch County became strong enough to produce damaging wind gust.
episodes.206227: Several clusters of thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours across southeast South Carolina near a stationary front and associated weak area of low pressure. These storms moved to the southwest along outflow boundaries and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.206254: Thunderstorms moved northward through Pima and Cochise counties and produced heavy rainfall with reported totals ranging from 0.10 to 1.0 inches. The heavy rainfall closed multiple roadways in Tucson, Saint David, Tombstone, and Sierra Vista.
episodes.206331: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the St Lucie and Martin County coasts.
episodes.206332: Locally heavy rainfall produced significant roadway flooding and led to a roof collapse of a community center in Melbourne.
episodes.206387: Thunderstorms occurred across southern MT and northern WY, producing large hail up to 2 inches in diameter and gusts up to 78 mph.
episodes.206417: Repeated rounds of rainfall from thunderstorms that developed in the afternoon and evening of July 22, 2025 over the Southeast Florida urbanized area.
episodes.206766: Hot and humid conditions resulted in a deeply unstable environment with SBCAPE of 3000-5000 J/kg and CAPE around 1000 J/kg as an MCV lifted across the area. Lack of deep layer shear prevented more organized storm development, though scattered convection did develop across the area through the afternoon and evening. One cell near Ottumwa produced gusty winds as the core collapsed, resulting in a gust of 62 mph at the Ottumwa ASOS.

South Carolina Highway Patrol confirmed that the crash involved 13 total vehicles, including 6 that were semi-trucks or other commercial vehicles.
